title: Encryption: Always Encrypted and column-level encryption
summary: Protect data at rest and in use with TDE, column-level encryption, and Always Encrypted (incl. secure enclaves).

items: Distinguish TDE, column-level encryption, and Always Encrypted.
Explain what Always Encrypted protects against and its client-driver requirement.
Describe secure enclaves for richer computations on encrypted data.

blocks.body: DP-800 emphasizes protecting sensitive columns. Always Encrypted is the headline: the server never sees plaintext or keys.

terms.definition: Transparent Data Encryption — encrypts data files at rest; transparent to queries.
Client-side encryption where keys never reach the server; protects data in use.
A protected memory region enabling comparisons/computations on Always Encrypted data.

blocks.heading: The three layers
blocks.body:
- **TDE** encrypts the whole database at rest, transparently.
- **Column-level encryption** uses keys/certificates via `ENCRYPTBYKEY`.
- **Always Encrypted** encrypts on the **client**; the engine stores and returns ciphertext and never has the Column Encryption Key. **Secure enclaves** extend it to support pattern-matching and range comparisons.

items.mistake: Expecting the server to query Always Encrypted columns in plaintext.
items.fix: Only enclave-enabled operations work server-side; otherwise decryption happens in the driver.

tips: 'Server admin/DBA must not see plaintext' => Always Encrypted.
Secure enclaves enable richer WHERE operations on encrypted columns.

blocks.body: Layer TDE (at rest), column encryption, and Always Encrypted (in use). Always Encrypted keeps keys client-side; enclaves add richer queries.
